issues.title: LO-32 — WebUI: wsBuffer_[] static member defined in header, ODR violation risk
issues.body:
Copied from https://github.com/JN0V/DomoticsCore/issues/187 for a trial of workline's line on this copy.

The WebUI component declares a static buffer, `wsBuffer_`, in a header. If the buffer is defined in the header too, each translation unit that includes it could get its own definition. That risks a linker error or silent duplicate state. The roadmap does not say which build shows it. It hurts anyone who builds the WebUI in a project with several source files.

<details><summary>For the builder</summary>`static char wsBuffer_[WEBUI_WS_BUFFER_SIZE];` and `bufferLock_` are declared in `DomoticsCore-WebUI/include/DomoticsCore/WebUI.h` (the class `WebUIComponent`). Check where each is defined.</details>

Opened from `docs/CODE-ROADMAP.md`, lines 6352 to 6352 by the product-owner role.

<!-- workline:import=docs/CODE-ROADMAP.md:2e2aab9c6fc4 -->

## Validation

- **Several source files:** Given two source files that both include `DomoticsCore/WebUI.h`, When the project is built and linked, Then the link succeeds with no duplicate-symbol error for `wsBuffer_` or `bufferLock_`.
- **One shared buffer:** Given a build with several source files that use the WebUI, When the poll handler and the live-update broadcast build an update, Then both use the same single buffer and the same single lock.

---

## Verification

- **Step 1, confirm the state.** Search the repository for the definitions of `WebUIComponent::wsBuffer_` and `WebUIComponent::bufferLock_`. The class in `DomoticsCore-WebUI/include/DomoticsCore/WebUI.h` only declares them (lines 82 and 83).
  - A definition that is plain, in the header and not `inline`: the defect is real. Fix it.
  - A definition that is `inline`, or sits once in a `.cpp`: no defect remains. A person closes the issue as obsolete. The checks below are then only a guard.
- **Link check.** Build two source files that both include `DomoticsCore/WebUI.h` for a board target, for example ESP32. Link them into one program. WebUI does not compile natively, so this needs the board toolchain. The link must succeed. A plain definition in the header makes it fail with a duplicate-symbol error.
- **One symbol each.** Run the board toolchain's `nm -C` on the linked program. `WebUIComponent::wsBuffer_` and `WebUIComponent::bufferLock_` must each show exactly one defined symbol.
- **One buffer and one lock.** Add a source check that runs in CI and needs no board. It reads `WebUI.h` and requires the following.
  - Exactly one definition of each of the two members.
  - Both the `/api/ui/updates` poll handler and the live-update broadcast take `bufferLock_` through a `LockGuard`.
  - Both use `wsBuffer_` and no other buffer.
  This fails if a user gets its own copy or skips the lock.
- Run the link check in the same CI job as the board build, so it keeps guarding later changes.

## Scope

Guessed: the lines holding the definitions of `wsBuffer_` and `bufferLock_` were not in the code given, so the exact place of the change is not confirmed.
- `DomoticsCore-WebUI/include/DomoticsCore/WebUI.h`: the two static members of `WebUIComponent` (declared at lines 82 and 83), their definitions, and the users of the buffer (the `/api/ui/updates` poll handler and the live-update broadcast).
- A new `.cpp` under `DomoticsCore-WebUI/src`, only if a single out-of-header definition is chosen over `inline`.
- A new check under `DomoticsCore-WebUI/test` or an example with two source files, plus the build or CI config that runs it.

## Assumptions

- Assumption taken on 2026-11-04, the Validation draft unanswered after 5 min: written as the role drafted it, for a person to correct.
